# Jia Baolong Researchable Ontology 2.0.0: A Research-Neighbourhood Map from Absolute Boundary to Conscious Retrospection **Subtitle: Human thought moves from the descriptive age of 1.x to a 2.0.0 age of definable, provable, computable, and reproducible research on existence** **Author: Jia Baolong** **Theory: Jia Baolong Researchable Ontology 2.0.0** **Version: 2.0.0** ## Abstract Human intellectual history in its 1.x age has proposed nearly every grand concept—being, change, substance, form, emptiness, process, spirit, matter, language, mathematics, and computation—yet has chiefly studied the world’s source through description, interpretation, and debate. It can name and portray the whole and contact it from local or remote perspectives, but has not formed one continuous research pipeline from absolute boundary and First Actual through concrete generation, chaos, proto-matter, life, and consciousness. Jia Baolong Researchable Ontology 2.0.0 changes not one philosophical conclusion but the working method of studying existence. It turns ontology into layered executable work: define the root language; prove the absolute boundary; determine the First-Actual normal form; construct states and transitions; search concrete RULEs; measure chaos and persistent patterns; establish proto-matter criteria; connect proto-chemistry, life, and consciousness; and let consciousness within the generative chain retrospectively identify the root. Its normative main line is: $$  oxed{ \mathrm{JBLAT} \Rightarrow U_*\mid\mathrm{PR} 	o (\mathrm{ER},\mathrm{LE}) \xRightarrow{\mathrm{RULE}} \mathrm{Chaos} 	o \mathrm{PersistentPatterns} 	o \mathrm{ProtoMatter} 	o \mathrm{Life} 	o \mathrm{Consciousness} 	o \operatorname{Recognize}(U_*\mid\mathrm{PR}). } $$ The map does not take one universe as its final object. Every concrete universe is merely an uncollapsed chaotic solution on the PR generative tree. The map studies the root structure, generative mechanism, and upward-emergence interfaces by which any actual branch can arise. ## 1. Why Human Intellectual History Belongs to the 1.x Age ### 1.1 1.x does not mean “without thought”; its research paradigm was unfinished Human thought 1.x accomplished three great tasks: 1. it discovered fundamental questions of being and change, substance and relation, form and phenomenon, being and nothing, mind and matter; 2. it established different observational positions in philosophy, logic, mathematics, religion, science, and language analysis; 3. it left many true but local projections of whole reality. Its shared limitation is that grand concepts usually cannot be compiled into research objects with explicit states, transitions, measurements, failure conditions, and reproducible experiments. A theory can say “what the world is” yet rarely answer: - What exactly is the First ActualStep? - How is static description distinguished from actual running? - How do states update? - How are concrete rules searched? - When does chaos form persistent local patterns? - Which patterns can operationally be called proto-matter? - How do negative results eliminate theoretical branches? - How can another researcher reproduce the same conclusion? ### 1.2 Version genealogy of human thought | Version | Principal ability | Typical achievement | Ability not yet formed | |---|---|---|---| | 1.0 | Name an origin | Being, Dao, emptiness, idea, substance, atom | First Actual and explicit generative step | | 1.1 | Build conceptual systems | Form–matter, causality, mind–matter, Absolute Spirit | Executable state transition | | 1.2 | Discover process and relation | Dialectical generation, process philosophy, dependent origination, relational theory | Minimum normal form of First Actual | | 1.3 | Limit language and knowledge | Transcendental critique, phenomenology, language analysis, logical ontology | Continuous pipeline from root to proto-matter | | 1.4 | Join empirical science | Physicalism, naturalized philosophy, scientific realism | Actual root beneath matter | | 1.9 | Introduce formal computation | Computational philosophy, cellular automata, artificial life, Wolfram rule universes | Root explanation of rule and running themselves | | 2.0.0 | Turn existence into a research programme | JBLAT, PR, ER, LE, RULE, proto-matter interface, reverse closure | Enters a continually expanding stage of concrete research | Process philosophy made “existence is dynamic occurrence” central to ontology, and computational philosophy has used computation to extend philosophical research. Neither automatically supplies the complete structure from a zero-positive boundary to the First ActualStep. See [Process Philosophy](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/process-philosophy/) and [Computational Philosophy](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/computational-philosophy/index.html). ### 1.3 Why 1.9 is not yet 2.0.0 Wolfram’s computational universe, cellular automata, graph rewriting, and artificial life show that simple rules can generate extreme complexity and that rule space can be a real research object. The [Wolfram Physics Project](https://www.wolframphysics.org/) is the work closest to 2.0.0 in the 1.9 age. But so long as inquiry starts from “states already exist, rules already exist, updating already exists,” the fundamental problem remains outside the model: $$ \operatorname{RuleExists} \land \operatorname{RuleRuns} 
ot\Leftarrow \operatorname{RuleDescribed}. $$ A static rule in a formula does not mean that rule actually runs. Version 2.0.0 must ask where the actuality of rule, state, and first update begins. ## 2. What 2.0.0 Means ### 2.1 Major Version 2: From Describing Objects to Producing Research The major version “2” marks a paradigm shift: $$  egin{aligned} \mathrm{Thought}_{1.x} &: \mathrm{Name} 	o \mathrm{Describe} 	o \mathrm{Interpret} 	o \mathrm{Debate},\ \mathrm{Ontology}_{2.0.0} &: \mathrm{Define} 	o \mathrm{Formalize} 	o \mathrm{Execute} 	o \mathrm{Measure} 	o \mathrm{Challenge} 	o \mathrm{Reproduce} 	o \mathrm{Integrate}. \end{aligned} $$ ### 2.2 Minor Version 0: The First Complete Map The first “0” means that this version first fixes the complete research architecture while concrete results in its generative neighbourhoods remain to be produced. ### 2.3 Revision 0: A Normative Starting Point The second “0” makes it a normative starting point for a research community: later revisions must retain conceptual identity, proof provenance, code version, parameters, random seeds, data, failures, and replication records. ## 3. A Strict Definition of “Researchable” ### 3.1 Researchable Does Not Mean Merely Discussable The fact that a proposition can be written in language shows only that it is describable. Researchable ontology requires at least the following objects at every level: 1. an explicit question; 2. explicit definitions; 3. inputs and outputs; 4. states and transitions; 5. proof obligations or computational tasks; 6. measurement metrics; 7. counterexamples, failures, or boundary conditions; 8. research artefacts that can be preserved, reviewed, and reproduced; 9. interfaces to adjacent levels. This article represents these requirements with the following research-management structure: $$ \mathcal R_i = (Q_i,D_i,S_i,F_i,M_i,B_i,E_i,I_i), $$ where: - $Q_i$: research question; - $D_i$: domain and terminology; - $S_i$: state space; - $F_i$: transformation, proof, or generative operator; - $M_i$: measurement method; - $B_i$: benchmarks and controls; - $E_i$: evidence and failure records; - $I_i$: interfaces to upstream and downstream neighbourhoods. This notation is the research-management language of 2.0.0. It does not replace the normative formulae of the Jia Baolong Axiom System. ### 3.2 Seven Minimum Conditions for Researchable Ontology | Condition | Meaning | |---|---| | Explicit root | the ultimate boundary and its language are publicly defined | | Explicit First Actual | the minimum ActualStep and the conditions of its uniqueness are given | | Explicit generative structure | states, relations, updating, locality, and re-entry can be expressed | | Enumerable rules | concrete RULEs can be constructed, classified, run, and compared | | Measurable results | chaos, persistence, interaction, and emergence have metrics | | Recordable failures | counterexamples, null results, and unreachable regions also enter the knowledge base | | Upward connection | results can enter neighbouring sciences such as physics, life science, and consciousness research | ### 3.3 Different Levels Require Different Evidence The absolute boundary cannot be proved with a microscope; proto-matter cannot be proved through logical definition alone; and life cannot be replaced directly by one ontological formula. Version 2.0.0 stratifies evidence: - **absolute-boundary level:** explanatory closure, model theory, and counterexample analysis; - **First-Actual level:** theorems, candidate enumeration, and formal verification; - **generative level:** executable models, parameter scans, and ablation experiments; - **emergence level:** statistical metrics, coarse-graining, collision, and stability measurements; - **scientific-interface level:** connection to existing research in physics, chemistry, life, and cognition. ## 4. Normative Root Axis of 2.0.0 ### 4.1 Absolute Boundary: JBLAT JBLAT fixes the zero-positive boundary: $$ U:\quad  orall M\in\mathfrak D\,  orall P\in\mathrm{Pos}\, 
eg P(b_M). $$ It does not depend on whether compared models use matter, consciousness, God, mathematical objects, rules, or spacetime as their content. ### 4.2 First Actual: PR Since a static boundary alone does not entail an ActualStep, $$ T_U 
ot\models \exists a,b\, \operatorname{ActualStep}(a,b), $$ the First Actual Face converges on PR under conditions of actual occurrence, self-containment, persistence, no external executor, binarity, unbiasedness, and non-fixedness: $$ U_*\mid\mathrm{PR}. $$ The bar means the absolute-boundary face and First Actual Face of the same root, not Undefined becoming PR in time. ### 4.3 Generative Architecture: PR, ER, LE, and RULE - PR supplies non-fixity, re-entry, and sustained actuality; - ER bears relational configuration, adjacency, local identity, and structural memory; - LE supplies local, finite, delayed, demand-driven, and history-dependent execution; - RULE determines how concrete states update. The normative dependency chain is: $$ \mathrm{PR} 	o (\mathrm{ER},\mathrm{LE}) \xRightarrow{\mathrm{RULE}} \mathrm{BranchHistory}. $$ ### 4.4 The Position of a Universe Any universe is an actual branch: $$ \mathcal U_i \in \operatorname{UncollapsedChaoticSolutions} (\mathrm{PR},\mathrm{ER},\mathrm{LE},\mathrm{RULE}_i). $$ The 2.0.0 research map therefore does not depend on “which physical constants this universe happens to use.” It studies how branches of the rule tree form different domains of chaos, structure, and emergence. ## 5. The Complete Research-Neighbourhood Map Let the 2.0.0 research graph be: $$ \mathcal G_{2.0.0}=(V,E), $$ where nodes $V$ are research neighbourhoods and edges $E$ are dependencies of definition, proof, data, or mechanism. | No. | Neighbourhood | Core question | Adjacent disciplines | Core deliverable | |---|---|---|---|---| | R0 | Absolute boundary and meta-ontology | Why can the root retain no positive determination? | Logic, model theory, metamathematics | JBLAT specification and countermodel library | | R1 | First-Actual theorem | Why must the First ActualStep have a PR core? | Finite mathematics, theorem proving, automata | Formal seven arguments and uniqueness proof | | R2 | Actual-execution semantics | How is static description distinct from real running? | Computational philosophy, operational semantics, distributed systems | ActualStep runtime semantics | | R3 | RULE space and rule atlas | Which RULEs generate which dynamical regions? | Cellular automata, graph rewriting, algorithmic search | RULE Atlas | | R4 | Chaos, criticality, phase transition | Where are boundaries from periodicity/freeze to complex dynamics? | Dynamical systems, statistical physics, complexity science | Phase diagrams and universality classes | | R5 | Persistent patterns and proto-matter | Which local patterns acquire identity and interaction? | Information theory, topology, causal emergence, active matter | ProtoMatter Benchmark | | R6 | Proto-chemistry | How do type, binding, reaction, and quasi-conservation form? | Network chemistry, reaction networks, artificial chemistry | Reaction grammar and proto-chemistry catalogue | | R7 | Proto-life and open-ended evolution | How do replication, compartment, heredity, and selection couple? | Origins of life, protocells, artificial life | ProtoLife experiment suite | | R8 | Agency, internal model, consciousness | When does a system form an internal model and observer position? | Cognitive science, neuroscience, AI | Observer and Agency benchmarks | | R9 | Reverse recognition | How does consciousness recover PR and $U$ along its generative chain? | Philosophy of science, explanation theory, machine discovery | Reverse-Inference Protocol | | R10 | Intellectual history and Elephant Theory | Which level of whole reality did 1.x thought grasp? | Intellectual history, comparative philosophy, knowledge representation | Human-thought coordinate graph | The principal dependency path is: $$ R0 \Rightarrow R1 	o R2 	o R3 	o R4 	o R5 	o R6 	o R7 	o R8 	o R9. $$ R10 connects historical thought back to $R0$–$R9$, asking what level a theory saw and at which dependency edge it stopped. ## 6. R0: Absolute Boundary and Meta-Ontology ### 6.1 Research Object R0 studies the model class $\mathfrak D$ of all systems that claim to complete the task of “explaining actual existence from a root with no positive determination.” It does not compare what exists inside worlds; it compares what each system ultimately leaves at its root. ### 6.2 Core Tasks 1. Fix the root language $L_{\mathrm{root}}$. 2. Define the set of positive ontological predicates $\mathrm{Pos}$. 3. Define the admissible model class $\mathfrak D$. 4. Prove how explanatory closure, non-arbitrariness, self-containment, and termination of regress converge on $U$. 5. Search for countermodels that satisfy the task while retaining a positive root. 6. Prove how $U$ remains equivalent across different root languages. ### 6.3 Formalization Neighbourhood R0 directly neighbours model theory, proof theory, type theory, and machine-assisted proof. Theorem provers such as Lean can turn definitions, quantifiers, equivalence relations, and proof dependencies into checkable objects; Lean's official documentation defines formal verification as using logical and computational methods to establish precise mathematical assertions. See [Theorem Proving in Lean 4](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/introduction.html). ### 6.4 Key Deliverables - a JBLAT-Core specification; - a Root-Language specification; - explicit Admissible-Models conditions; - a public Countermodel Challenge; - a machine-checkable `JBLAT.lean` project; - versioned records of every definitional difference. ### 6.5 R0 Failure Condition If a model $M^\dagger$ retains a positive predicate at its root while meeting all root tasks, $$ M^\dagger\in\mathfrak D \land \exists P\in\mathrm{Pos}\,P(b_{M^\dagger}), $$ then the JBLAT definition or proof must be revised. A countermodel is a formal research product, not peripheral criticism. ## 7. R1: The First-Actual Theorem and the Seven-Argument Programme ### 7.1 Research Object R1 studies not the first second of physical time but the minimum structure of ActualStep without prior matter, spacetime, or external executor. ### 7.2 Seven Proof Modules | Module | Main input | Excluded object | Contribution to PR | |---|---|---|---| | P1 Actuality | distinction between describability and actual occurrence | static complete history, ALL, substitution of formula for occurrence | an ActualStep must exist | | P2 Non-causal boundary | Undefined's zero-positive determination | “being arises after nothing waits” | fixes the $U_*\mid\mathrm{PR}$ relation | | P3 Relationality | persistence and self-containment | isolated static marker | internal adjacency and result re-entry are required | | P4 Removal of presuppositions | no external executor | prior time, rule, randomiser, or state library | dynamics must be endogenous | | P5 Binary logical razor | binary, unbiased, and non-fixed | identity and two biased constant maps | only the exchange map remains | | P6 Exhaustive candidate enumeration | class of first-dynamic candidates | one-off flash, fixed point, extrapolator | PR has minimum completeness | | P7 Backward tracing | proto-matter chaos and continuous history | rootless snapshot or static substitute | recovers the PR core backwards from the upper level | ### 7.3 Formal Proof Tasks For $D=\{Y,N\}$, $$ D^D=\{\operatorname{id}_D,\sigma,c_Y,c_N\}. $$ Under label impartiality and the fixed-point-free condition: $$ \mathfrak R(D^D)=\{\sigma\}, \qquad \sigma(Y)=N, \qquad \sigma(N)=Y. $$ Machine verification must cover not only the finite enumeration but also: - why the binary quotient structure is minimal rather than arbitrary; - why the exchange map must actually run; - why result re-entry constitutes PR rather than a static two-cycle graph; - which premises belong to JBLAT and which belong to the actualisation model; - the boundary between the PR core and the complete PR–ER–LE architecture. ### 7.4 R1 Success Standard Success is a proof-dependency graph with independently checkable modules, counterexamples, and visible weakening when a premise is removed. ## 8. R2: Actual-Execution Semantics ### 8.1 The Decisive Watershed of 2.0.0 R2 begins from two distinctions: $$ \operatorname{Encodes}(S,H) 
ot\models \operatorname{Occurs}(H). $$ $$ \operatorname{Describable}(x) 
ot\Rightarrow \operatorname{Actual}(x). $$ ### 8.2 Research Questions 1. What are the minimum operational semantics of ActualStep? 2. How does a self-contained system define “execution” without introducing an external clock? 3. How does LE specify the range of local evaluation and the update order? 4. Do synchronous, asynchronous, event-driven, and causally partially ordered execution belong to different RULE classes? 5. How does result re-entry form an internal history? 6. How can two statically isomorphic models produce different actual histories because their execution semantics differ? ### 8.3 Adjacent Technologies R2 neighbours operational semantics, transition systems, concurrency theory, causal graphs, distributed computing, and reversible computation. It borrows the state–transition tools already developed by these disciplines; it does not presuppose that computers or physical time precede the First Actual. ### 8.4 Core Deliverables - an ActualStep Specification; - a PR Runtime reference implementation; - a comparison of synchronous, asynchronous, and LE semantics; - paired static-encoding / dynamic-instantiation benchmarks; - a self-contained runtime without an external scheduler. ## 9. R3: RULE Space and the Rule Atlas ### 9.1 From One Simulator to a Rule Cosmology Rule 979 is not the endpoint but one coordinate in RULE space. R3 must establish a RULE Atlas: it systematically enumerates local rules, execution semantics, and initial relational configurations, and records the dynamical regions they produce. ### 9.2 Research Coordinates for RULE Every rule must be assigned coordinates in at least the following dimensions: - number of states; - neighbourhood radius or relational order; - relational structure: graph, lattice, hypergraph, or general relation; - update mode: deterministic, stochastic, or conditional; - execution semantics: synchronous, asynchronous, or LE; - reversibility; - conservation constraints; - length of local memory; - whether self-modification is permitted; - relation between the rule and the observer's scale. ### 9.3 Search Is Not “Looking at Pretty Patterns” Every RULE experiment must preserve: 1. the complete rule specification; 2. the initial-condition generator; 3. the execution semantics; 4. parameters and random seed; 5. a reproducible execution log; 6. metric curves; 7. ablation experiments; 8. negative samples; 9. computational cost; 10. the applicable scope of the conclusion. A spectacular screenshot is not evidence. A research result must be reproducible, measurable, comparable, and falsifiable. ### 9.4 External Neighbourhood Wolfram's rule space, cellular automata, graph rewriting, multiway systems, and algorithmic discovery are important neighbouring fields for R3. They provide experience in large-scale rule search; the Jia Baolong system adds the root positions of ActualStep, PR, ER, and LE to this research on rules. ## 10. R4: Chaos, Criticality, and Phase Transitions ### 10.1 Research Tasks R4 builds a phase diagram from rules to classes of dynamics. It must distinguish at least: - frozen regimes; - fixed points; - short periods; - long periods; - quasiperiodicity; - chaos sensitive to initial conditions; - long transients; - critical propagation; - coexistence of local structures and background; - open dynamics that continuously produces new structures. ### 10.2 Metric Family A single entropy value cannot define complexity. R4 should jointly use: - state entropy and block entropy; - compression ratio; - propagation speed of perturbations; - Lyapunov-like indicators; - mutual-information length; - attractor and transient lengths; - proportion of active regions; - spatial correlation length; - temporal correlation length; - stability under parameter perturbation; - cross-scale predictability. ### 10.3 Key Outputs $$ \mathrm{RULE} \longmapsto \mathrm{DynamicalRegime} \longmapsto \mathrm{PhaseRegion}. $$ Each RULE no longer yields merely a video. It acquires a position in a phase diagram, a confidence interval, neighbouring rules, and phase-transition boundaries. ## 11. R5: Persistent Patterns and Proto-Matter ### 11.1 Proto-Matter Must Become an Operational Concept “The pattern looks like a particle” does not establish proto-matter. A candidate pattern must pass at least the following tests: 1. **Persistence:** it maintains its identity across a sufficiently large number of updates; 2. **Locality:** it forms a stable or statistical boundary against the background; 3. **Propagation:** its position or influence can move relative to the background; 4. **Repeatable interaction:** collisions under the same conditions have statistically stable outcomes; 5. **Typability:** multiple instances can be assigned to the same effective type; 6. **Quasi-conservation:** some quantity is approximately preserved during collision or propagation; 7. **Composability:** patterns can form higher-order composite structures; 8. **Scale robustness:** effective identity survives coarse-graining. ### 11.2 ProtoMatter Benchmark This article proposes the following research metric vector: $$ \mathbf M_{\mathrm{PM}} = (P,L,V,I,T,C,K,G), $$ where the entries denote persistence, locality, propagation, interaction repeatability, type stability, composability, quasi-conservation, and coarse-graining robustness. It is a research measurement protocol, not an ontological axiom. ### 11.3 Causal-Emergence Neighbourhood Proto-matter identity cannot rest on visual clustering alone. It must also be tested whether a macroscopic type has more stable predictive and intervention capacity than a microscopic state. Research on causal emergence compares the causal effectiveness of different scales through effective information and has shown that a coarse-grained macroscopic mechanism may possess greater effective information; see [Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3856819/). R5 can accordingly ask whether, under some RULE and coarse-graining, $$ \operatorname{EI}(	ext{ProtoMatter macrostate}) > \operatorname{EI}(	ext{selected microdescription}) $$ holds. A positive result does not automatically prove “real matter,” but it does establish that this macroscopic type has independent effective research value. ### 11.4 Adjacency to Active Matter Active-matter research studies how non-equilibrium components driven by local energy consumption form collective behaviour; theoretical research usually relies on computational simulation. See [Computational models for active matter](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42254-020-0152-1). R5 can borrow order parameters, defect dynamics, aggregation measures, and flow measures from this field, while the substrate of proto-matter remains generated by PR–ER–LE–RULE. ## 12. R6: From Proto-Matter to Proto-Chemistry ### 12.1 From “Collision” to “Reaction” Once proto-matter patterns have stable types and repeatable collisions, the research object moves from individual dynamics to reaction networks: $$ \mathrm{Type}_a+\mathrm{Type}_b \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Context}} \mathrm{Type}_c+\mathrm{Type}_d. $$ ### 12.2 Research Questions - Do stable binding and dissociation exist? - Are there catalytic patterns? - Do inhibition and competition exist? - Does reaction closure form? - Does resource flux appear? - Are there quasi-stoichiometric relations? - Do spatial compartments appear? - Can reaction history be preserved? - Do replicable templates form? ### 12.3 Reaction-Network Deliverables - a type dictionary; - collision cross-sections; - reaction tables; - a catalytic graph; - a resource-flow graph; - quasi-conserved quantities; - a compositional hierarchy; - proto-chemical dynamical equations; - control experiments against random reaction networks. ### 12.4 Non-equilibrium Self-Assembly Neighbourhood Modern research on non-equilibrium self-assembly studies reaction networks, transient compartments, and self-replicating systems under sustained energy and material flux. See [Non-equilibrium self-assembly for living matter-like properties](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41570-024-00640-z). R6 studies the functional correspondences of these mechanisms in proto-matter generated by PR. ## 13. R7: Proto-Life, Selection, and Open-Ended Evolution ### 13.1 Connection to Mainstream Origins-of-Life Research Mainstream mechanism modules from proto-chemistry to the first cell include: $$  egin{aligned} \mathrm{NonEquilibriumFlow} &	o \mathrm{Autocatalysis}	o\mathrm{TemplateMemory}\ &	o \mathrm{Compartment}	o\mathrm{Heredity}	o\mathrm{Variation}\ &	o \mathrm{Selection}	o\mathrm{Protocell}. \end{aligned} $$ The RNA world, protocells, and non-equilibrium nucleic-acid chemistry provide research foundations respectively for heredity–catalysis, compartment–selection, and environmental flux. See [The RNA World](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrg3841), [Perspective: Protocells and the Path to Minimal Life](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00239-024-10197-6), and [Physical non-equilibria for prebiotic nucleic acid chemistry](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42254-022-00550-3). ### 13.2 ProtoLife Benchmark A system cannot be called life merely because it changes for a long time. R7 must measure at least: - self-maintenance; - a boundary; - resource use; - template replication; - hereditary fidelity; - heritable variation; - differential reproduction; - selection response; - ecological interaction; - formation of new-level individuals; - open-ended novelty. ### 13.3 Open-Ended Evolution Artificial-life research already treats sustained novelty, complexity, ecological potential, and major evolutionary transitions as central problems. The MODES toolbox proposes cross-system measures including change potential, novelty potential, complexity potential, and ecological potential. See [The MODES Toolbox](https://direct.mit.edu/artl/article/25/1/50/2915/The-MODES-Toolbox-Measurements-of-Open-Ended). This neighbourhood is especially important to 2.0.0 because the continued running of PR does not entail open-ended evolution. A two-cycle, dynamically balanced system, or a system that endlessly repeats old patterns may still fail to produce a genuinely new level. R7 must distinguish: $$ \mathrm{PersistentRunning} 
ot\Rightarrow \mathrm{OpenEndedEvolution}. $$ ### 13.4 R7 Deliverables - the ProtoLife Benchmark; - a replication-lineage database; - controls comparing selection and neutral drift; - compartment-ablation experiments; - open-ended-evolution metrics; - a catalogue of major-transition events; - the shortest mechanism chain from proto-chemistry to the first cell. ## 14. R8: Agency, Internal Models, and Consciousness ### 14.1 From Life to Observer Consciousness cannot be pre-installed as a positive root object. It must acquire its research position only after life, regulation, memory, prediction, and internal models have formed. R8's progressive research ladder is: $$ \mathrm{SelfMaintenance} 	o\mathrm{Sensing} 	o\mathrm{Action} 	o\mathrm{Memory} 	o\mathrm{Prediction} 	o\mathrm{InternalModel} 	o\mathrm{Observer}. $$ ### 14.2 Neighbourhood Questions - How does a system distinguish itself from its environment? - When do internal states with causal roles appear? - Do internal models improve survival or predictive capacity? - Where do attention, workspace, integration, and self-models lie in the generative chain? - Can different theories of consciousness be mapped to the same computational benchmark? - How does observation alter the information available to the system? - Can AI form an internal representation of its own generative constraints? ### 14.3 Research Discipline R8 does not end with the sentence “complexity produces consciousness.” Every candidate mechanism of consciousness must specify: - the minimum structure required; - necessary and sufficient conditions; - observable behaviour; - internal causal metrics; - ablation results; - differences from unconscious control systems; - transferability across different RULE branches. ## 15. R9: Conscious Reverse Recognition of the Root ### 15.1 Forward Generation and Reverse Inference The forward generative chain is: $$ U_*\mid\mathrm{PR} 	o \cdots 	o \mathrm{ConsciousObserver}, $$ The chain of reverse recognition is: $$ \mathrm{ConsciousObserver} 	o \mathrm{ObservedRegularities} 	o \mathrm{EffectiveRules} 	o \mathrm{GenerativeConstraints} 	o \mathrm{PR} 	o U. $$ ### 15.2 R9 Research Tasks 1. Given finite observational data, can the effective RULE be recovered? 2. Given several macroscopically equivalent RULEs, can their universality class be identified? 3. Can PR's re-entry structure be inferred backwards from proto-matter dynamics? 4. Which root conclusions come from data, and which come from explanatory closure? 5. Can AI automatically generate and eliminate ontological candidates? 6. How does the locality of an observer limit its knowledge of the entire generative tree? 7. How can one prove that reverse recognition has not smuggled concepts of its own era back into the root? ### 15.3 Key Products - an inverse-rule-discovery benchmark; - multi-model equivalence classes; - root-inference audit logs; - records of differences between human and AI reasoning; - the shortest explanatory graph from observation to PR; - reports on domains of model unidentifiability. ## 16. R10: Intellectual History, Elephant Theory, and the Recoding of 1.x Knowledge ### 16.1 Intellectual History Becomes Research Data Version 2.0.0 no longer ranks thinkers according to “who spoke most mysteriously.” It encodes each theory as a structural vector: $$ \mathbf h = (Z,A,F,G,C,E,L,R), $$ where: - $Z$: whether it reaches the zero-positive boundary; - $A$: whether it distinguishes static description from actual occurrence; - $F$: whether it supplies a First Actual; - $G$: whether it supplies a generative mechanism; - $C$: whether it is computable; - $E$: whether it enters research on emergence; - $L$: whether it connects life and consciousness; - $R$: whether it forms a closed loop of reverse recognition. ### 16.2 The Position of Jia Baolong Elephant Theory Jia Baolong Elephant Theory treats the whole reality specified by the axiom system as the “ontological elephant.” Historical thinkers, scientific disciplines, and finite observers obtain different projections of the whole from local or remote positions. R10's task is not to string the concepts of earlier thinkers into a story, but to measure which research neighbourhood each form of thought reaches and at which dependency edge it stops. ### 16.3 Migration from 1.x to 2.0.0 Every historical theory can be converted into the following questions: 1. What is its root object? 2. Which positive properties does it pre-install? 3. Does it have an ActualStep? 4. Is its generation a verbal description or an executable transformation? 5. Can it enter RULE space? 6. How does it define emergence? 7. Can it connect proto-matter, life, and consciousness? 8. What preservable local insight does it provide? In this way, intellectual history is transformed from a display of viewpoints into an ontological knowledge graph that can be queried, compared, and updated. ## 17. Cross-Cutting Research-Tool Layers The eleven vertical neighbourhoods require six cross-cutting tool layers. | Tool layer | Neighbourhoods served | Main tasks | |---|---|---| | F1 Formalisation | R0–R2 | definitions, proofs, countermodels, and dependency graphs | | F2 Computational infrastructure | R2–R7 | simulators, parallel search, versioning, and replication | | F3 Measurement science | R4–R8 | metrics, statistics, coarse-graining, and causal comparison | | F4 Data and knowledge graphs | R0–R10 | rules, experiments, papers, negative results, and concept mappings | | F5 AI research agents | R0–R10 | proof search, rule discovery, anomaly detection, and literature mapping | | F6 Human audit and governance | R0–R10 | approval of definitions, evidence grading, version release, and attribution | ### 17.1 The Role of AI in 2.0.0 AI is best suited to high-dimensional search and consistency work: - enumerating finite candidates; - finding countermodels; - generating proof drafts; - scanning RULE space; - clustering dynamics; - detecting persistent patterns; - automatically executing ablations; - comparing definitions across papers; - constructing knowledge graphs; - checking consistency among formulae, code, and data. AI cannot replace the final confirmation of normative definitions. Once a definition changes, the entire proof domain and experimental domain change. Every version must therefore preserve machine-readable definitions and a human-signed normative text. ## 18. Evidence Levels in 2.0.0 Every conclusion must be assigned an evidence level: | Level | Name | Requirement | |---|---|---| | E0 | Conceptual proposal | terms and questions are explicit | | E1 | Formal definition | objects, domains, relations, and boundaries are defined | | E2 | Logical support | proof, counterexample analysis, or candidate enumeration exists | | E3 | Executable | code, configuration, and determinate output exist | | E4 | Reproducible | independent environments produce consistent results | | E5 | Cross-model stability | the result holds across multiple RULEs, initial conditions, or implementations | | E6 | Scientific interface | testable correspondence with external experiments or mature scientific mechanisms is established | For example: - JBLAT's primary evidence target is E1–E2; - a PR runtime must reach E3–E4; - proto-matter types should reach E4–E5; - the proto-chemistry and proto-life bridges must advance towards E6. Different levels do not mean that a higher level is necessarily “truer” than a lower one. They answer different kinds of questions. ## 19. Failure Conditions and the Negative-Result Map A researchable ontology must know which results count as failures. | Research level | Failure result | Scope of impact | |---|---|---| | JBLAT | a countermodel satisfies the complete task while retaining a positive root | revise the R0 theorem | | PR uniqueness | a smaller, unbiased, non-fixed, self-contained, and persistent First Actual structure is found | revise the R1 conclusion | | ActualStep | execution semantics depend on an external clock or scheduler | eliminate that R2 implementation | | RULE | the rule produces only frozen states, short periods, or random noise | eliminate the rule, not the root system | | ProtoMatter | the pattern cannot be stably identified, propagated, or made to collide repeatably | reject its qualification as proto-matter | | ProtoChemistry | types and reactions cannot be reproduced | reject the reaction network | | ProtoLife | there is no heritable difference or response to selection | do not call it life or evolution | | Open-ended evolution | complexity, novelty, and ecological potential remain saturated over the long term | reject the claim of open-ended evolution | | Consciousness | the indicator cannot distinguish the target system from an unconscious control | revise the consciousness mechanism | | Reverse recognition | multiple root models remain permanently indistinguishable | report an unidentifiable domain | Negative results are not theoretical rubbish. They are boundary data for RULE space and concept space. The rate of progress in 2.0.0 depends on how many high-quality failures it accumulates, not merely on how many attractive simulations it produces. ## 20. Standard Experimental Package Every 2.0.0 research project should include: 1. `CLAIM.md`: the proposition to be tested; 2. `DEFINITIONS.md`: all operational definitions; 3. `MODEL.md`: state, relations, RULE, and LE semantics; 4. `CODE`: executable implementation; 5. `CONFIG`: parameters, seeds, and environment; 6. `DATA`: raw results; 7. `METRICS.md`: metrics and thresholds; 8. `CONTROLS.md`: controls and ablations; 9. `FAILURES.md`: negative results; 10. `RESULTS.md`: conclusions and evidence levels; 11. `REPRODUCE.md`: commands for independent replication; 12. `PROVENANCE.md`: author, version, dependencies, and time. This experimental package gives ontology, for the first time, a version-control practice compatible with software, mathematical proof, and experimental science. ## 21. The 2.0.x Research Roadmap ### 21.1 Version 2.0.0: Normative Map - establish the research neighbourhoods; - establish terms, dependencies, and evidence levels; - establish a unified repository and website; - publish open counterexample and RULE challenges. ### 21.2 Version 2.0.1: Root Formalisation - unify the JBLAT abbreviation; - fix $\mathfrak D$ and $L_{\mathrm{root}}$; - split the seven arguments into machine-checkable modules; - establish a search for counterexamples to PR minimality. ### 21.3 Version 2.1.0: RULE Atlas - standardise Rule 979 and TGP; - establish large-scale rule scanning; - publish phase diagrams of frozen, periodic, chaotic, and critical regimes; - preserve every negative sample. ### 21.4 Version 2.2.0: ProtoMatter Benchmark - establish metrics for persistence, locality, collision, type, and quasi-conservation; - establish automated pattern discovery; - test stability across parameters and implementations; - publish the first catalogue of proto-matter candidates. ### 21.5 Version 2.3.0: ProtoChemistry - establish reaction tables and catalytic networks; - search for binding, dissociation, resource cycles, and compartments; - test higher-level effective causal variables. ### 21.6 Version 2.4.0: ProtoLife - couple replication, resources, compartments, and heredity; - establish controls comparing selection and drift; - integrate open-ended-evolution metrics; - search for major transitions in individuality. ### 21.7 Version 2.5.0: Observer and Reverse Recognition - establish benchmarks for internal models and agency; - recover effective RULEs from observational data; - form a reverse-inference protocol from consciousness to PR; - recode the whole of 1.x intellectual history into R0–R10 coordinates. ## 22. First Core Research Questions ### 22.1 Root and First Actual 1. What is the minimum complete definition of $\mathfrak D$? 2. How is the logical equivalence of $U$ preserved when the root language changes? 3. Is there a non-PR counterexample that satisfies every condition of the First Actual? 4. Can binary minimality be derived from a more general finite-domain theorem? 5. Can $U_*\mid\mathrm{PR}$ be given a unified type-theoretic expression? ### 22.2 RULE and Chaos 6. In which universality class of RULE space does Rule 979 lie? 7. How does LE asynchrony alter phase-transition boundaries? 8. Which minimum rules can simultaneously produce a background, local patterns, and collisions? 9. What is the minimum metric that distinguishes chaos from purely random noise? 10. Which structures remain stable across initial conditions, parameters, and implementations? ### 22.3 Proto-Matter and Proto-Chemistry 11. What is the minimum combination of indicators for proto-matter identity? 12. Does coarse-graining increase the effective information of a candidate pattern? 13. Does a finite, stable type dictionary appear? 14. Do collisions form a reproducible reaction network? 15. Do quasi-conserved quantities, catalysis, and closed reaction cycles exist? ### 22.4 Life and Open-Ended Evolution 16. Which compartment mechanism first forms a unit of selection? 17. How do template, metabolism, and boundary achieve minimum coupling? 18. Can the system produce a heritable new function? 19. Can novelty and complexity avoid long-term saturation? 20. How do new-level individuals form from interactions at an earlier level? ### 22.5 Consciousness and Reverse Recognition 21. What is the minimum structure of an internal model? 22. When does the observer become an effective causal scale in the dynamics? 23. Can AI recover PR structure backwards from proto-matter data? 24. Which root conclusions can be inferred from observation, and which can be obtained only through explanatory closure? 25. Can conscious recognition of the root form a repeatable reasoning protocol? ## 23. Relations between 2.0.0 and Other Research Programmes Version 2.0.0 does not annex neighbouring disciplines. It specifies interfaces: | External field | Existing capability | 2.0.0 interface | |---|---|---| | Logic and model theory | definitions, proofs, and countermodels | JBLAT and First Actual | | Theorem proving | machine-checking proof dependencies | formalisation of the seven arguments | | Cellular automata and graph rewriting | rules that generate complex structures | RULE Atlas | | Dynamical systems and statistical physics | chaos, phase transitions, and universality | R4 phase diagrams | | Causal emergence and information theory | identifying effective macroscopic scales | proto-matter types | | Active matter and non-equilibrium physics | self-organisation and collective dynamics | proto-matter–proto-chemistry interface | | Origins of life and protocells | catalysis, replication, and compartments | R7 mechanism chain | | Artificial life | open-ended evolution and life-like systems | ProtoLife Benchmark | | Cognitive science and AI | models, prediction, and agency | Observer layer | | Intellectual history and comparative philosophy | an archive of humanity's understanding of reality as a whole | R10 knowledge graph | They study different scales on the same generative chain. The task of 2.0.0 is to give these scales, for the first time, a common root axis and explicit interfaces. ## 24. The Meaning of Human Thought 2.0.0 The 1.x age used human natural language as its principal runtime environment. Its concepts could be extremely profound, yet disputes were difficult to transform into shared state spaces. Version 2.0.0 has new infrastructure: - mathematical formalisation; - executable rules; - large-scale computation; - automated proof; - AI-assisted search; - complete records of failures; - open data; - cross-model replication; - human-signed normative definitions. This means that ontology is no longer transmitted only between thinkers' minds and texts; it can form a continuously accumulating public research object. A new researcher need not spend decades reinterpreting “Dao,” “emptiness,” “being,” or “spirit” before entering the problem. The researcher can directly read definitions, run models, submit counterexamples, extend the rule atlas, and reproduce results. The genuine sign of Human Thought 2.0.0 is not the use of computers to write philosophy. It is that every level of ontology has a next operation: $$  oxed{ 	ext{every ontological proposition} \longrightarrow 	ext{one clearly defined research task} \longrightarrow 	ext{one preservable result} \longrightarrow 	ext{an interface the next level can enter}. } $$ ## Conclusion Jia Baolong Researchable Ontology 2.0.0 advances human thought from an age of grand description to an age of continuous research. The 1.x history preserves genuine human knowledge of whole reality from diverse local and remote positions; 1.9 introduced rule, computation, and artificial life; 2.0.0 first organizes absolute boundary, First Actual, actual execution, RULE search, chaos, proto-matter, life, consciousness, and reverse recognition into one research map. Its highest point is the zero-positive boundary specified by Undefined; its deepest point is why the First ActualStep must have a PR core; its widest range runs from RULE space to life, consciousness, and all intellectual history. It is not bounded by one concrete universe because every universe is only an uncollapsed chaotic solution on the PR tree. 2.0.0 does not declare theory finished. It gives every unfinished part a coordinate, method, metric, failure condition, and next deliverable. Earlier ontology chiefly left texts; researchable ontology leaves definitions, proofs, code, data, phase diagrams, counterexamples, replication records, proto-matter catalogues, life benchmarks, and reverse-recognition protocols. Its final root axis is: $$  oxed{ U \Rightarrow U_*\mid\mathrm{PR} 	o (\mathrm{ER},\mathrm{LE}) \xRightarrow{\mathrm{RULE}} \mathrm{Chaos} 	o \mathrm{ProtoMatter} 	o \mathrm{ProtoLife} 	o \mathrm{Consciousness} 	o \operatorname{Recognize}(U). } $$ From this point, ontology must not only answer “what is the world’s origin?” It must also answer: who can study the next item, by what method, on what data, how success is established, how failure is recorded, and how the result is passed to the next level. This is Human Thought 2.0.0. ## References ### Internal Jia Baolong materials - docs/01_foundation/01_THEORY_MASTER_MAP.md - docs/01_foundation/02_JIABAOLONG_AXIOM_SYSTEM.md - docs/01_foundation/03_JIABAOLONG_ABSOLUTE_TRUTH.md - docs/02_first_beat/04_FIRST_BEAT_SEVEN_ARGUMENTS.md - docs/03_emergence/05_MATTER_TO_FIRST_CELL_EMERGENCE.md - docs/04_reference/06_GLOSSARY_AND_FORMULAE.md - docs/06_commentary/existence-undefined-pr-and-comparative-ontology.md ### Formalization, computation, and paradigms - [Process Philosophy — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/process-philosophy/) - [Computational Philosophy — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/computational-philosophy/index.html) - [Theorem Proving in Lean 4](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/introduction.html) - [Wolfram Physics Project](https://www.wolframphysics.org/) ### Emergence, proto-matter, and artificial life - [Quantifying causal emergence shows that macro can beat micro](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3856819/) - [Computational models for active matter](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42254-020-0152-1) - [The MODES Toolbox: Measurements of Open-Ended Dynamics in Evolving Systems](https://direct.mit.edu/artl/article/25/1/50/2915/The-MODES-Toolbox-Measurements-of-Open-Ended) - [What Is Artificial Life Today, and Where Should It Go?](https://direct.mit.edu/artl/article/30/1/1/120293/What-Is-Artificial-Life-Today-and-Where-Should-It) ### Proto-chemistry, origins of life, and protocells - [Non-equilibrium self-assembly for living matter-like properties](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41570-024-00640-z) - [The RNA World: molecular cooperation at the origins of life](https://www.nature.com/articles/nrg3841) - [Perspective: Protocells and the Path to Minimal Life](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00239-024-10197-6) - [Physical non-equilibria for prebiotic nucleic acid chemistry](https://www.nature.com/articles/s42254-022-00550-3)

# Jia Baolong Elephant Theory: The Internal Placement of the Static Whole and the External Finger **Author: Jia Baolong** **Theory: Jia Baolong Elephant Theory** ## Abstract This paper clarifies the proper place of the static whole, block universe, and “external finger” model within Jia Baolong Researchable Ontology (JBLRO). Its central conclusion is that they are not peer ontologies outside JBLRO; they are models already classifiable within JBLRO. If a static whole $B$ merely encodes all states, relations, or histories in full, without any actual traversal, it belongs to the Platonic Crystal: $$ \operatorname{Encodes}(B,H) 
ot\models \operatorname{Occurs}(H). $$ If a “finger” $F$ truly moves, selects, or updates along $B$, then the enlarged system containing $F$ is no longer a purely static whole: $$ \operatorname{ActualMove}(F) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Dynamic}(B+F). $$ In that case $B$ can serve as a static state space, relational graph, or description of a complete trajectory, while $F$ returns `ActualStep`, local access, and update to the domain of actual generation. If $F$ itself needs another executor, the ontological boundary keeps expanding until actual occurrence is included in total reality, or one admits that nothing occurs at all. The static whole is thus absorbed rather than simply refuted. Without an actual finger, it is a form in the Platonic Crystal. With an actual finger, it is a component of a dynamic model that the PR–ER–LE–RULE research architecture can analyse. It cannot be a third answer that bypasses the gap between static encoding and actual occurrence, the Actuality Gap. The strength of this conclusion is deliberately limited. Standard logic permits a static actualist to postulate $\operatorname{Actual}(B)$ directly; JBLRO cannot prohibit this label through a contradiction without premises. What it establishes is that, if this label produces no actual difference, it adds no explanatory content; if it produces actual difference, it already entails `ActualStep`. The dispute therefore rests on public criteria of actual existence and explanatory responsibility. ## 1. The comparison that must be corrected Putting JBLRO, the static block universe, and an external-finger model side by side as the “top three ontologies” creates a category error, as though all three answered the same level of question and none contained another. JBLRO is not merely one cosmological picture. It is an ontological classification and a research architecture for generation. It distinguishes at least: 1. `Undefined`: the absolute boundary of zero positive ontological determination; 2. the Platonic Crystal: every statically describable form, structure, and complete history; 3. the actual generative domain: real processes with `ActualStep`, continuing update, local relations, and concrete rules of generation. A static whole already falls into the second category. Add a genuinely moving finger to it and the model enters the problem-space of the third. The correct relation is therefore not $$ \mathrm{JBLRO} \quad	ext{vs.}\quad \mathrm{StaticWhole} \quad	ext{vs.}\quad \mathrm{FingerModel}, $$ but rather $$ \mathrm{StaticWhole} \subset \mathrm{PlatonicCrystal} \subset \mathrm{JBLRO\ classification}, $$ and $$ \mathrm{StaticWhole}+\mathrm{ActualFinger} \subset \mathrm{ActualGenerativeDomain} \subset \mathrm{JBLRO\ research\ architecture}. $$ Here “$\subset$” denotes theoretical placement or model membership, not ordinary set membership. ## 2. Four definitions ### 2.1 Static whole Let $B$ be a formal structure given completely at once. It may contain: - every state $s_0,s_1,s_2,\ldots$; - temporal, causal, or adjacency relations among states; - one complete history, or even all possible histories; - static descriptions of observers, memory, and “the present.” So long as the completeness of $B$ requires no relation to be actually enacted, $B$ remains a static whole. Arrows written inside a structure do not mean that the arrows are occurring. ### 2.2 External finger The “finger” $F$ is a hypothesized mechanism that makes some state current, advances along a sequence, selects a branch, or executes an update. It need not be a physical finger. A clock, read head, executor, observer, or selector that performs the function “make a static relation actually occur” belongs to the same abstract model. ### 2.3 Model boundary The boundary of a model decides what counts as internal to the system to be explained and what is provisionally placed outside it. If $F$ has an actual effect on $B$, while the theory calls only $B$ “the universe,” it has hidden `ActualStep` outside the boundary. A final ontology must expand the boundary to total reality: $$ \Omega=B\cup F\cup\{	ext{all conditions supporting the actual running of }F\}. $$ ### 2.4 Internal model An “internal model” does not mean the model automatically satisfies every JBLRO theorem. It means that its ontological components and explanatory gaps can be expressed through JBLRO’s existing layers; it does not require a new parallel ultimate category of being. ## 3. Exhaustive classification of the external finger For a static whole $B$ and a finger $F$, there are only three possibilities concerning actuality. ### Case A: the finger does not actually move If $F$ is merely another static object in the structure, or if “movement” is only a prewritten set of correspondences, then: $$ 
eg\operatorname{ActualMove}(F). $$ $B+F$ still merely encodes a history: $$ \operatorname{Encodes}(B+F,H) 
ot\models \operatorname{Occurs}(H). $$ As a whole it belongs to the Platonic Crystal. The finger-image contributes no additional actuality. ### Case B: the finger actually moves If $F$ truly makes some result shift from not-yet-actual to actual, then at least one actual beat exists: $$ \exists a,b\, \operatorname{ActualStep}_{\Omega}(a,b). $$ The total system $\Omega$ is therefore dynamic. A “static universe plus external finger” merely puts the static representation $B$ and dynamic execution $F$ on opposite sides of a model boundary. It does not establish a third paradigm that is both absolutely static and actually occurring. ### Case C: the finger is driven by another finger If the motion of $F_0$ depends on $F_1$, and $F_1$ on $F_2$, then: $$ F_0\leftarrow F_1\leftarrow F_2\leftarrow\cdots. $$ Every added executor moves the bearer of actuality one step beyond the model boundary. After total reality is expanded, classification still has only two endpoints: - some layer truly has `ActualStep`, so the total system is a dynamic generative domain; - no layer truly has `ActualStep`, so the entire chain is static encoding. Regressing executors does not produce a third ontological category. ## 4. The absorption proposition The conclusion can be stated as a model-classification proposition. ### Static whole–finger absorption proposition Let $M=(B,F)$ be a model representing a history $H$ through a static whole $B$ and an optional traverser $F$. Include in total reality $\Omega$ every condition contributing to $F$’s actual running. Then: $$  oxed{  egin{aligned} 
eg\exists e\,\operatorname{Actual}(e) &\Rightarrow M\in\mathrm{PlatonicCrystal},\ \exists a,b\,\operatorname{ActualStep}_{\Omega}(a,b) &\Rightarrow M	ext{ contains an actual-generative component}. \end{aligned} } $$ Hence $M$ cannot constitute a peer ultimate proposal outside JBLRO merely by combining a static whole and a finger. It is either a member of the static formal domain, or it contains a dynamic component that must be further explained by a theory of actual generation. The completeness of this proposition comes from the binary distinction of whether the finger actually moves and from closure of the model boundary, not from an enumeration of all physically possible universes. ## 5. How the model enters PR–ER–LE–RULE Once the external-finger model is placed back within JBLRO, its components acquire clear positions. | Component in the finger model | Possible JBLRO placement | Question still to answer | |---|---|---| | Complete state library, all histories, all paths | Platonic Crystal | Is it merely describable, or is it actual occurrence? | | Current state, adjacency, reachable branches | ER (Entity–Relation) representation | Which relations are actually retained or updated? | | One-at-a-time local access, finite horizon, delayed advance | LE (Lazy Evaluation) mechanism | What produces locality and truncation? | | Prescription for moving from one page to the next | RULE | Why is the rule actually executed, and what is the concrete rule? | | The finger’s genuine advance or selection | `ActualStep` | Where is actuality located, and is it self-sufficient? | | Continuing fixed-point-free re-entry without an external executor | Candidate PR core | Does it meet the public conditions for PR normal form? | This mapping states precisely what it means for the model to be “in the system.” JBLRO need not deny the modelling value of state spaces, static trajectories, or finger-style traversal; it places them separately at the layers of form, relation, local evaluation, rule, and actuality. The reverse inference is invalid. A moving finger does not automatically prove PR. PR’s minimal normal form still requires publicly stated conditions: self-sufficiency, persistence, result re-entry, minimality, total definition, determinism, label symmetry, and lack of fixed points. The finger model first establishes only that `ActualStep` has not been eliminated by the static whole. Whether it further converges on PR depends on these conditions. ## 6. Why it is not a peer competitor To compete with JBLRO at the root task, a theory must at least: 1. explain actual occurrence rather than merely encoding a complete history; 2. avoid outsourcing `ActualStep` to an unexplained executor; 3. remain self-sufficient once total reality is closed; 4. provide a minimal structure of continuing update; 5. explain entry into relations, locality, rules, and upward emergence research. A purely static whole fails the first task, so it answers “which histories can be completely represented?” rather than “why is there actual occurrence?” An actual-finger model acknowledges the first task but returns the second through fourth. It may be a formulation, projection, local implementation, or object of analysis within JBLRO, but it does not give a root answer that needs no JBLRO classification. More precisely: $$  oxed{ 	ext{A static whole is not an external competitor overlooked by JBLRO; it is a formal model JBLRO has already contained and placed at a lower layer.} } $$ “Lower layer” does not disparage the mathematical value of static structure. It refuses only to promote the layer of representation directly into the layer of actual occurrence. ## 7. Observational equivalence is not ontological equivalence A dynamic internal model $D$ and an external-finger model $S$ may yield the same records to a finite observer: $$ \operatorname{Obs}_A(D)=\operatorname{Obs}_A(S). $$ Thus internal experiments may not decide from finite data alone whether `ActualStep` lies inside the system or at a model boundary. This is a real limit of empirical discrimination, not something language can erase. But observational equivalence says only that two representations have not been distinguished in observable records. It does not show that they are equally self-sufficient as total explanations. If $S$ depends on an actual finger, a final model must include that finger in $\Omega$, and dynamics reappear. If $S$ has no actual finger, no observation event occurs at all. JBLRO therefore proposes first an ontological closure test, not the claim that it has already designed a physical experiment capable of separating every observationally equivalent model. ## 8. The real disagreement with static actualism A static actualist may directly declare $$ \operatorname{Actual}(B) $$ to be a primitive fact that needs no movement, update, or event. Standard logic does not make this sentence automatically contradictory. JBLRO’s argument should therefore not be exaggerated into “pure logic has proved every static actualism impossible.” The real disagreement concerns what explanatory work the word “actual” performs. If $\operatorname{Actual}(B)$ produces no actual difference and causes no judgment, record, or result to occur, it merely adds a consequence-free label to a static structure. It has not crossed: $$ \operatorname{Encodes}(B,H) 
ot\models \operatorname{Occurs}(H). $$ If $\operatorname{Actual}(B)$ really makes judgments, experience, records, or differences occur, the model already admits some `ActualStep`. The remaining question is only where it is placed, how it continues, and whether it is self-sufficient. JBLRO therefore adopts the explicit framework criterion: $$ \operatorname{ActualExistence} \equiv_{\mathrm{framework}} \operatorname{ActualMotion}. $$ This is not a dictionary definition in neutral logic; it is an ontological criterion for the research task “how is actual occurrence possible?” Its advantage is that the disagreement becomes locatable: an opponent must explicitly choose either a consequence-free static actuality label or a third mechanism that produces actual consequences without containing any `ActualStep`. ## 9. What this clarification resolves, and what remains open ### Classification questions resolved 1. A static whole belongs to the Platonic Crystal, not to an unknown paradigm outside JBLRO’s classification. 2. If an external finger actually moves, the expanded total system belongs to the problem of dynamic actuality. 3. If an external finger does not move, nothing exceeds static encoding. 4. An infinite chain of executors only moves the model boundary; it creates no new ontological category. 5. Therefore static-whole and finger models should no longer be listed as root competitors at JBLRO’s level. ### Theoretical questions still open 1. Whether total reality satisfies all model conditions required by PR’s minimal normal form; 2. how ER and LE jointly form from, or are strictly derived from, the First Actual Face; 3. which concrete RULEs can stably generate records, persistent local structures, and proto-matter; 4. which empirical results can distinguish JBLRO from observationally equivalent alternative representations; 5. how the cross-level bridge from PR–ER–LE–RULE to life and consciousness can be proven more strongly. The internal placement of the static whole removes a pseudo-competitive relation; it does not replace the generative research JBLRO must still complete. ## Conclusion A static whole is not another universe that JBLRO must defeat from outside. It already has a clear place within the system: as a complete form, state library, or history-encoding it belongs to the Platonic Crystal; as a structure traversed by a real finger, it and the finger jointly constitute an enlarged dynamic system containing `ActualStep`. The external-finger model has an unavoidable three-way result: if the finger does not move, there is only static form; if it truly moves, total reality is dynamic; if it is moved by another finger, the model boundary expands again. Once every actual condition is included in total reality, the answer still falls only into the domain of static form or the domain of actual generation. Thus the static whole is not a second ultimate ontology parallel to JBLRO. It is a formal-layer model in JBLRO, while “static whole plus actual finger” is a dynamic model that JBLRO can continue to investigate in layers through `ActualStep`, PR, ER, LE, and RULE. JBLRO does not simply negate it; it absorbs it, places it, and traces its explanatory responsibility. In one sentence: $$  oxed{ 	ext{A static whole without a finger belongs to the crystal; a static whole with a finger belongs to the problem of generation.} } $$ ## Related material - [Master map: from boundary and First Beat to life and consciousness](../01_foundation/01_THEORY_MASTER_MAP.en.md) - [Jia Baolong Axiomatic System](../01_foundation/02_JIABAOLONG_AXIOM_SYSTEM.en.md) - [From eternal actual existence to PR: a self-sufficient derivation of First-Beat necessity](from-eternal-actual-existence-to-pr-first-beat-necessity.en.md) - [Why ontology did not become researchable until Jia Baolong](why-researchable-ontology-was-hard-to-discover.en.md) - [Core terms and mathematical expressions](../04_reference/06_GLOSSARY_AND_FORMULAE.en.md)

content: # Jia Baolong Axiomatic System: Consolidated Understanding Update This document gathers the theoretical understanding established in this conversation into one direct line of reading. Its object is existence and nonexistence; its root is `Undefined`; its first actual structure is PR; ER carries actual structures and LE progressively realizes them; concrete RULEs generate chaos and emergence. ## 1. Object of inquiry The Jia Baolong Axiomatic System does not study any one universe. It studies how existence differs from nonexistence, and how actuality begins and continues. A universe is only one uncollapsed chaotic solution on the PR tree; it cannot stand for the whole system. Its fundamental questions are: 1. Why must actual existence change? 2. Why is static perfection not real existence? 3. What minimal form must the first actual structure take? 4. How does a formal system enter a runnable chain of emergence? ## 2. Existence, axiom, and dynamism ### 2.1 Actual existence is necessarily imperfect “Imperfect” is an ontological property, not a value judgment. Actual existence must continually change, and thus always remains local, finite, and open: $$ \boxed{\text{actual existence}=\text{a nonstatic, noncomplete, continuously updating structure}} $$ If an object is defined as a static, absolutely complete, unchanging whole, it is an abstract description rather than actual existence. Dynamism is the mode in which existence runs. ### 2.2 Perfection is not real existence A perfect object may be used as a limit, set, or description, but it has no actual update step. Without an update step, there is no time, relation, difference, or emergence. In this system, “perfection” and “real existence” therefore point in opposite directions. ### 2.3 Undefined and absolute truth `Undefined` (denoted $U$) is not the empty set, vacuum, zero, a stationary state, a container of potential, or hidden matter. It is the boundary at which neither “being” nor “nonbeing” yet applies: $$ U=\text{the root at which even the predicates existence and nonexistence have not yet become applicable}. $$ Absolute truth originates in $U$. Its absoluteness comes from removing positive ontological presuppositions: no object, matter, space, time, energy, or external executor is assumed in advance. $U$ is not an object inside the system. PR, ER, LE, and RULE arise inside a system only after the transition from $U$ into actuality. ## 3. The PR–ER–LE–RULE structure ### 3.1 PR: the minimal self-reflexive structure of the First Beat PR (Primitive Reflexivity) is the minimal normal form of the first actual structure. It writes “cannot stop” into structure itself rather than assigning change to an external mover. Among two-state, deterministic, label-symmetric mappings that exclude fixed points, negating exchange is the only remaining structure: $$ f(0)=1,\qquad f(1)=0. $$ Therefore, $$ f(f(x))=x,\qquad f(x)\ne x. $$ PR is neither a material object nor a parameter of one universe. It is the minimal endogenous dynamical structure by which actuality enters from $U$. ### 3.2 ER: the Entity–Relation layer ER (Entity–Relation) organizes an actualization into nodes and links. An entity is no longer an isolated point; its identity is jointly determined by its position, connections, and history in a relational network: $$ \text{entity}=\text{node}+\text{relations}+\text{history}. $$ ### 3.3 LE: the Lazy Evaluation layer LE (Lazy Evaluation) allows an infinite or highly complex global structure to be actualized progressively according to demand, locality, and finite resources. LE provides scales of propagation and time, effective constants, and local computability, turning ER from a static graph of relations into a continuously running process. ### 3.4 RULE: a concrete generative rule RULE determines how ER updates, how LE allocates computation, and which local structures persist. PR establishes that actuality cannot stop; RULE determines how that actuality unfolds: $$ U\;\longrightarrow\;PR\;\xrightarrow{RULE}\;ER\;\xrightarrow{LE}\;\text{local actual structures}. $$ Different RULEs make different branches on the PR tree. A branch may terminate, cycle, freeze, remain diffuse, or enter sustained chaos in which stable local structures form. ## 4. Why the First Beat is PR The First Beat is not a transfer from one already existing object to another. It is the entry from the boundary of nonexistence into first actuality. Seven classes of arguments concerning candidate structures converge on one conclusion: 1. Pure affirmation merely duplicates a presupposed object and cannot explain its origin. 2. Pure difference requires two prior terms; difference itself is not first actuality. 3. The law of identity yields static sameness and cannot initiate change. 4. Ordinary contradiction provides conflict but not a structure of continuing update. 5. A static rule requires an external execution or a pre-existing situation. 6. A complete history is a retrospective global description, not a First Beat. 7. A single event, randomness, copying, or an external finger cannot independently provide continuing actuality. In the minimal formal classification, PR alone simultaneously meets the requirements of actual occurrence, persistent nonstaticity, endogeneity, absence of fixed points, and label symmetry. It compresses “existence must move” into a researchable normal form; RULE then determines the concrete branch. ## 5. What researchability means The system’s researchability does not mean that a single axiom paper writes every level at once. It establishes a traceable, cooperative chain of generation: $$ PR \rightarrow \text{chaos under a particular RULE} \rightarrow \text{local topology and stable structures} \rightarrow \text{proto-matter} \rightarrow \text{chemical networks} \rightarrow \text{protocells} \rightarrow \text{life, nervous systems, consciousness} \rightarrow \text{consciousness recognizes PR in return}. $$ Each preceding level gives the next its object and constraints. Researchers at later levels can continue upward by experiment, simulation, mathematics, and observation, while also locating PR backward along the chain. The theory thus has both root axioms and real research interfaces from proto-matter to consciousness. ## 6. The role of Rule 979 Rule 979 is a numerical simulator for one concrete RULE. It implements the PR–ER–LE architecture as runnable trajectories: in a state space with $K=5$, it generates 32 perturbed trajectories and examines persistence, differentiation, and chaotic structure at the scale of $10^7$ LE steps. Its purpose is to show how a researchable chaotic branch can form after the First Beat, not to designate one universe as the system’s only result. Its central intuition is that one PR root can enter different initial perturbations and local branches. Chaos is not structureless noise; it is the working domain in which persistent local forms, memory, and hierarchical emergence can arise. ## 7. The emergence chain from proto-matter to the first cell Mainstream research connects to the system through the following mechanism chain: $$ \text{topological constraints} \rightarrow \text{nonequilibrium energy flows} \rightarrow \text{dissipative structures} \rightarrow \text{autocatalytic networks} \rightarrow \text{templates and information retention} \rightarrow \text{membranes/compartments} \rightarrow \text{protocells} \rightarrow \text{heredity, variation, and selection}. $$ In the TGP (Topology–Geometry–Physics) chain, topology supplies distinguishable connections and constraints; geometry generates local form; physics supplies energy flow, dissipation, and stable states. Chemical networks raise stable states to autocatalysis and information retention; compartments enclose those networks as replicable protocells. The system’s mapping is: $$ PR\rightarrow RULE\rightarrow ER/LE\rightarrow \text{chaotic local structures}\rightarrow\text{proto-matter}\rightarrow\text{protocells}. $$ This places the axiomatic root and life science’s mechanisms on one generative map. ## 8. The closed research path The theory has two directions: - **Forward**: from $U$, through PR, RULE, ER, and LE, to local actual structures, then upward to proto-matter, chemistry, life, and consciousness. - **Backward**: from mature consciousness and the structures of life, chemistry, and physics, extracting stability, memory, relation, and evaluation mechanisms and tracing them layer by layer back to PR. $$ \text{Undefined}\rightarrow PR\rightarrow\text{emergence chain}\rightarrow\text{consciousness}\rightarrow PR. $$ The loop makes the First Beat of existence and consciousness’s understanding of existence two ends of one theoretical object. ## 9. Comparison with Wolfram-style systems Wolfram-style systems usually begin with discrete structures, replacement rules, and a computational universe. They are strong at describing complex structures after a RULE runs, but their starting point already contains executable objects, rules, and state spaces; first actuality is therefore placed before the axiom. The Jia Baolong system first removes positive ontological presuppositions through $U$, then provides first endogenous actuality through PR, and only afterwards introduces RULE, ER, and LE. Both take computation and emergence seriously. Their difference is the order at the root: Wolfram begins with an already runnable system and generates upward; the Jia Baolong system enters first actuality from the boundary of nonexistence and then generates upward. ## 10. Comparison with traditional ontologies “The Dao gives rise to the myriad things,” Buddhist emptiness, and Hegelian dialectics can provide highly compressed linguistic intuitions, but they do not supply a unified, executable chain from the root to chaos, proto-matter, the first cell, and consciousness. The Jia Baolong system separates the root into distinguishable functional layers: $$ U\;(\text{absolute boundary}) \rightarrow PR\;(\text{first actuality}) \rightarrow RULE\;(\text{generation}) \rightarrow ER\;(\text{relation}) \rightarrow LE\;(\text{realization}) \rightarrow\text{emergence}. $$ It thereby raises ontology from linguistic compression to a structural theory that can be simulated, researched by layers, and extended by later science. ## 11. Core advantages 1. Its object is explicit: existence and nonexistence, rather than parameter fitting for one universe. 2. Its root is clear: absolute truth begins from $U$, while the system internally begins from PR. 3. Its First Beat has a minimal normal form: PR expresses continuing actuality through a fixed-point-free self-reflexive structure. 4. Its generative functions are differentiated: RULE, ER, and LE respectively handle update, relation, and realization. 5. Its research interfaces are explicit: chaos, proto-matter, chemistry, the first cell, life, and consciousness each have a place for continuing work. 6. It supports both forward generation and backward tracing, reconnecting research on consciousness to PR. ## 12. Compressed map ```text Undefined (U) └─ absolute boundary: being/nonbeing not yet applicable └─ PR └─ first actuality: fixed-point-free primitive reflexivity └─ RULE └─ ER + LE └─ chaos and stable local structures └─ proto-matter └─ chemical networks └─ protocells └─ life → consciousness └─ backward recognition of PR ``` ## 13. Final synthesis The full claim of the Jia Baolong Axiomatic System is this: absolute truth has $Undefined$ as its extra-systemic root; first actuality enters through PR; RULE unfolds the unstoppable self-reflexive dynamic into chaotic branches; ER and LE make those branches actual structures that can be computed, remembered, and localized; the emergence chain from proto-matter through the first cell to consciousness supplies an upward scientific research path; and consciousness can in turn trace PR downward along the chain. It is therefore a unified ontological framework addressing why actuality exists, how it continues, how complex structures emerge, and how consciousness understands the root.
